# Settings

<!-- Generated by scripts/build.ts from the defaults the modules register with defineConfig. Do not edit: change the
     default (and the comment on it) in the source file named under each group, then run `bun scripts/build.ts`.
     tests/unit/integration/config.test.ts fails when this file and the sources disagree. -->

Every default that shapes what Mimir draws is a named setting. A setting is read in one way
(`model.config('pace.play')`), and can be changed in three places. The nearest one wins:

1. **A scene**: `scene({ title, defaults: { pace: { play: 1.5 } } }, s => { … })`, or `s.config({ 'pace.play': 1.5 })`
   on the first line of the builder (what was created before the call keeps the old value, and `check` says so).
   `s.config('pace.play')` reads the value in force.
2. **A project**: `mimir.config.json` at the project root: `{ "defaults": { "pace": { "play": 1.5 } } }`. The CLI
   hands it to the viewer (`?config=<url>`; an export carries it inline). Other top-level keys of the file belong
   to the CLI.
3. **The default** registered by the module that owns the setting (the tables below).

Groups nest and keys may be written dotted: `{ pace: { play: 1.5 } }` and `{ 'pace.play': 1.5 }` are the same.
A value is plain data (a number, a text, true / false, null or a list), never a function: time is not an input here.
An unknown key, or a value of the wrong type, is a diagnostic with the nearest name (`API-UNKNOWN`, `API-TYPE`,
`NUM-INVALID`); the default stays in force. Keys of a module that is not loaded in the viewer are judged by
`mimir check`, which knows every module of the build.

360 settings in 6 groups: [`pace`](#pace) · [`camera`](#camera) · [`text`](#text) · [`guide`](#guide) · [`viewer`](#viewer) · [`look`](#look).

## pace

Registered in `src/core/rate.ts`.

| Setting | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `pace.enter` | `1` | appear, disappear, draw on, grow |
| `pace.write` | `1` | write a short text |
| `pace.writeLong` | `2` | write a text of 15 glyphs or more |
| `pace.transform` | `1` | turn one object into another |
| `pace.play` | `1` | one play: m.to.…, param.to(v) |
| `pace.sweep` | `3` | a step whose only content is a parameter sweep (st.set) lasts this long |
| `pace.sweepMin` | `2` | a step with a parameter sweep lasts at least this long, whatever else it plays |
| `pace.camera` | `2` | a camera move (st.camera, st.zoom) |
| `pace.wait` | `1` | st.wait() without a number |
| `pace.hold` | `1` | every step ends on a hold of this length |
| `pace.lag` | `0.1` | stagger of lagged(): the next member starts this share of the previous one's duration later |
| `pace.empty` | `1` | a step that records nothing still lasts this long (before its hold) |
| `pace.still` | `4` | a scene without steps plays for this long |
| `pace.scopedIn` | `0.4` | step-scoped marks (focus, labels) fade in over this long |
| `pace.scopedOut` | `0.4` | step-scoped marks clear over this long at the start of the next step |
| `pace.chapterFade` | `0.5` | when a chapter opens, one object takes this long to leave |
| `pace.chapterClear` | `0.8` | when a chapter opens, the whole clear (lagged fades, camera reset) takes this long |
| `pace.handoff` | `0.8` | live viewer: after a camera drag, the story's camera takes over again over this long |

## camera

Registered in `src/core/camera.ts`.

| Setting | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `camera.fov` | `30` | vertical field of view, degrees |
| `camera.view` | `"iso"` | the named view the camera looks from until a step says otherwise: iso, front, back, side, left, right, top, bottom |
| `camera.fill` | `0.8` | share of the 3D panel the model fills when the camera fits it on its own |
| `camera.fitFill` | `0.6` | share of the panel the named parts fill with st.camera({ fit: [parts] }) |

## text

Registered in `src/core/text.ts`.

| Setting | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `text.size.hero` | `90` | one line that owns the frame |
| `text.size.title` | `72` | the title of a scene |
| `text.size.section` | `60` | a section heading |
| `text.size.body` | `48` | running text: the size of a text that names none |
| `text.size.label` | `36` | a name beside a part |
| `text.size.note` | `24` | a remark, an axis label |
| `text.size.tiny` | `16` | the smallest size that still reads at 720p |

## viewer

Registered in `src/host/index.ts`.

| Setting | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `viewer.autoplay` | `true` | start playing as soon as the scene is ready (never in headless mode; `?autoplay=0` / `?autoplay=1` decide for one page; a page opened at a moment with `t=` or `step=` stays there; a person who asked for reduced motion is not played at unless the page says autoplay=1) |
| `viewer.mode` | `"video"` | the mode the viewer opens in (`?mode=` decides for one page); the player defines the modes, 'video' plays the story full-bleed |
| `viewer.speed` | `1` | story seconds per second of wall time while playing |
| `viewer.maxStep` | `0.1` | the most story time one displayed frame may advance, in seconds: a tab that was in the background resumes where it was instead of jumping |
